problem: The caption says flash/ROM is 'the only level that keeps code without power', but the same stack puts NAND flash and an SD card below it, and Section 1 correctly says those are non-volatile too. A student will read the caption as a contradiction.
fix: Say 'the only level in the top three that keeps data without power' (registers, SRAM, DRAM all lose it), or 'the working set that keeps code without power'.

where: Figure, item order against the side labels 'faster, costlier per bit' (top) and 'slower, cheaper per bit' (bottom)
problem: Flash/ROM is placed above DRAM, which under these labels claims that NOR flash random reads are faster than DRAM reads. In practice a DRAM read is faster (tens of nanoseconds) than a NOR flash random access, typically 70–120 ns. The stack mixes a volatility/role axis with a pure speed axis without saying so.
fix: Either put DRAM above flash/ROM on the speed scale, or state in the caption that the middle rungs are ordered by role (code vs working data), not strictly by read speed, and that NOR flash reads are close to, but slower than, DRAM.

problem: '1000 writes/s would wear a 10⁴-cycle block in about 10 s' silently assumes one block erase per write. A real logger fills a sector with many 4-byte samples before erasing, so the erase rate, and therefore the wear time, is smaller by the number of samples per block.
fix: State the assumption: 'at one erase per second (one erase per write) a 10⁴-cycle block is gone in 10⁴ s; erasing even once per second wears it out in under three hours, and logging every millisecond with an erase per write kills it in about 10 s.'
